correctness.rationale: The Latin condition makes row, column and symbol adjacency types exclusive on edges. A clique containing three in a line cannot extend outside it, and a nonline four-clique has a proper three-edge-coloring with opposite edges of each color; row and column matchings yield the alternating rectangle. A mixed triangle determines at most one such completion. Descending anchor-pair removals leave the line 2-skeleton portions with every edge and only anchor triangles; a mixed facet of each intercalate tetrahedron is free. This leaves n^2 vertices, 3n binomial(n,2) edges and 3n binomial(n-1,2)+n^2(n-1)-I(M) triangles. Symbol edges can be replaced across mixed triangles by two rook edges. Rectangles with a symbol diagonal are filled by two triangles. Without a diagonal, the two auxiliary cells are distinct from the corners and each other; the six displayed faces give the rectangle as boundary, with 7 interior edges and cyclic links at both interior vertices (a subdivided disk). Mapping the two-skeleton of the product of simplices into the flag complex using these fillings contracts all rook loops, since attaching cells above dimension two does not change pi_1. The reduced 2-complex is then simply connected with free H_2 of rank chi-1; Hurewicz and homological Whitehead give the wedge. The proof's reference to a 'four-simplex' for the four-vertex intercalate is a dimension typo, not an extra coface or a failure of the collapse.
residual_risks: Only the claimed nonequivariant homotopy type for Latin squares is verified; no conclusion for additional parallel classes or homotopy actions.
